walkthroughs.body_html:
Component 01: Portfolio — a core area of GCSE Art & Design.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Component 01: Portfolio brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Component 01: Portfolio.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which technique uses crossing lines for tone?
options: Stippling
Cross-hatching
Smudging
Tracing
Lines
Dots
Circles
Squares

mcqs.q: Why is understanding patronage important for studying historical art?
options: Artists worked freely - patronage was irrelevant to the artwork.
Patrons commissioned art for specific purposes, shaping content and form.
A composition with no balance.
Patrons painted the works themselves.

mcqs.q: What are the three primary colours in paint (subtractive)?
options: Red, green, and blue.
Black, white, and grey.
Red, yellow, and blue (or magenta, yellow, cyan in print).
Patrons painted the works themselves.
A composition with no balance.
An unbalanced composition.
Visual equilibrium achieved with different elements of equal visual weight on each side.
Patrons painted the works themselves.
